question: The suspension of funding to UNRWA by several EU Member States is seriously imperilling its ability to continue providing humanitarian aid in Gaza. UNRWA is the only agency able to reach and provide services to and operations for the civilian population of a territory entirely besieged by the occupying state of Israel.

The European Commission's barely credible, reckless official statement of 29 January 2024 only adds to the uncertainty surrounding the EU's commitment to this agency, which may collapse if its contributing countries and organisations continue to withhold funding.

Europe must set an example in terms of solidarity and assist those suffering genocide in Gaza and refuse to accept the rhetoric of a state such as Israel, which has been discrediting the agency’s work for years.

Does the Commission intend to maintain and increase humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza, as per the measures ordered by the International Court of Justice, and ensure humanitarian aid reaches them while Israel’s brutal massacre remains ongoing, killing more than 26 000 people so far, destroying infrastructure and laying siege to an entire area?
answer: The EU has stressed that the services the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) provides in Gaza and across the region are essential (1). The Commission has welcomed the United Nations (UN) Office of Internal Oversight Services investigation to shed light into the serious allegations against UNRWA staff.

Furthermore, it has commended the UN for creating an independent review group led by former French Minister Catherine Colonna to assess whether the Agency is doing everything within its power to ensure neutrality and respond to allegations of serious breaches (2). The Commission has engaged with UNRWA Commissioner-General and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake.
Letters outlining the way forward with all the measures and procedures for the Commission’s conditional funding for UNRWA were exchanged on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The conditions for the disbursement of the first tranche were the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the department of internal investigations and ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen Department of Internal Oversight Services, including the establishment of a new neutrality investigation unit and ethics office.

Following UNRWA’s fulfilment of these conditions, the Commission paid a first tranche of EUR 50 million out of the EUR 82 million foreseen for UNRWA for 2024. The second and third tranches of EUR 16 million respectively are subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.
Furthermore, the Commission has allocated over EUR 290 million in humanitarian aid for Palestinians since the beginning of the conflict.

EU humanitarian aid to Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank continues unabated through partner organisations, and also includes a further contracting of EUR 16 million (separate from the payments described above) that UNRWA received from the Commission’s humanitarian aid budget for food, medical and non-food items, shelter, as well as education and psycho-social support to civilians in Gaza.
